newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Daewoo explores hi-tech Australia deals.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo explores hi-tech Australia deals.

text.p: South Korean conglomerate Daewoo Electronics Co, a unit of the Daewoo industrial group, said it wanted to tap into Australian electronic research and development expertise to help expand its presence in local and Asian consumer electronic products markets.
"We already supply private brands here (in Australia) but we will now start our own brand campaign," Daewoo Electronics chairman Soon-Hoon Bae told reporters on Thursday.
"We would like to be introduced to some high-tech companies here. Australia has the potential to become a high-tech market," Bae said after a business luncheon.
Bae said it was too early to consider setting up manufacturing facilities in Australia.
"I am interested in the possibility but not yet. I have no special plan."
Daewoo was in Australia to start its own brand sale campaign in electronic consumer products, particularly television receivers, Bae said.
Daewoo currently sold about US$32 million worth of private brand electronic products to local retailers and had about three percent of the Australian market.
The company had no acquisition plans in Australia but aimed to lift its share of national sales to about 10 percent eventually, Bae said.
The Australian consumer electronics market was small in relation to global markets, he said.
"But Australia has many high-tech companies and Australia can become an important supplier of both software and hardware products."
